subject: English
passage: Although fossil evidence confirms that giant ground sloths once roamed the southern forests of South America, paleontologists have debated whether the animals inhabited these woodlands year-round—the so-called permanent residence scenario—or merely passed through them on seasonal migrations between distant grasslands. Researchers Ashok Hayashi and Dong-Hyun Ito recently contributed to this debate by analyzing oxygen isotope ratios preserved in fossilized tooth enamel recovered from a Pleistocene cave deposit in Patagonia. Hayashi and Ito concluded that the permanent residence scenario is likely correct.
prompt: Which finding about the tooth enamel, if true, would most directly support Hayashi and Ito's conclusion?

choices.A: Its mineral structure indicates that it is unlikely to have been altered by chemical processes after the sloths' deaths.
choices.B: It contains isotope signatures suggesting that the animals consumed forest vegetation across all seasons of the year over many years of life.
choices.C: Its isotope composition is most consistent with the animals having spent only brief intervals feeding within the forest before moving on.
choices.D: It shows wear patterns that could have resulted either from browsing on woody plants or from grazing on tough grasses.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. This choice provides direct support for the researchers' conclusion. If the tooth enamel shows isotope signatures indicating the sloths consumed forest vegetation across all seasons over many years, that supports the "permanent residence scenario," which proposes that the animals inhabited the woodlands year-round (and not merely during seasonal passages).

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. This choice does not support the researchers' conclusion, but rather the opposite. Animals having spent only "brief intervals" feeding in the forest before moving on aligns with the opposing seasonal-migration scenario, not with the permanent residence scenario the researchers endorse.
